name: Antigravity CLI

versions_seen.where: agy -p runs on macOS in a scratch git folder (probe:versions/1.5.14/hook-calls-print.jsonl)

cocheck_relevance: Calls arrive as PreToolUse and PostToolUse with a call id, and a failed edit shows in PostToolUse's error field. CoCheck reads Antigravity through a manifest only (public-kit/harness/harnesses/antigravity/), so its credit basis is inferred. Gaps: a failing shell command looks like a success, a denied call has no Post, and a helper's calls cannot be tied to the main session.

install.claim: The command is agy; the recording was made with 1.5.14 on macOS.

available.claim: agy 1.5.14 ran command hooks from a workspace file, <folder>/.agents/hooks.json, in print mode with the folder trusted.

config.claim: Hooks live in a hooks.json that maps a hook name to its events. PreToolUse and PostToolUse take groups (matcher plus hooks); SessionStart, PreInvocation, PostInvocation and Stop take handler objects directly. A single entry carrying both shapes was read once per event, by the shape that event takes.
The global hooks file is ~/.gemini/config/hooks.json. This path is read from Antigravity's documentation and no recording has exercised it; the workspace file takes the same entries.
config.note: The documentation page was not re-fetched for this entry.

trust_or_approval.claim: The recording trusted the scratch folder through --settings (session only). A call the headless permission check denies gets a PreToolUse and nothing after it: no PostToolUse and no Stop.

fact.claim: SessionStart fired once per conversation in the 1.5.14 recording.
fact.note: can_block and can_rewrite are false because the schema wants a boolean here; whether Antigravity lets this hook block or rewrite is not known (see open_questions).

fact.claim: PreInvocation fired before every model call with invocationNum and initialNumSteps (numbers).
fact.note: can_block and can_rewrite are false because the schema wants a boolean here; whether Antigravity lets this hook block or rewrite is not known (see open_questions).

fact.claim: PostInvocation fired after every model call.
fact.note: can_block and can_rewrite are false because the schema wants a boolean here; whether Antigravity lets this hook block or rewrite is not known (see open_questions).

fact.claim: PreToolUse carries toolCall (id, name, args) and stepIdx.
fact.note: can_block and can_rewrite are false because the schema wants a boolean here; whether Antigravity lets this hook block or rewrite is not known (see open_questions).

fact.claim: PostToolUse carries the same toolCall.id as its Pre, and error: empty, or the tool's own words when the tool failed. No result.
fact.note: can_block and can_rewrite are false because the schema wants a boolean here; whether Antigravity lets this hook block or rewrite is not known (see open_questions).

fact.claim: Stop carries terminationReason, fullyIdle, continuationActive, executionNum and error. No closing message.
fact.note: can_block and can_rewrite are false because the schema wants a boolean here; whether Antigravity lets this hook block or rewrite is not known (see open_questions).

call_ids.claim: toolCall.id is sent on both PreToolUse and PostToolUse of a call.

session_files.claim: Every payload carries transcriptPath and artifactDirectoryPath. CoCheck does not read the transcript.

helpers_or_subagents.claim: A helper started by invoke_subagent runs under its own conversationId with an empty lastUserInput and no field naming its parent; the only link is the Recipient of the helper's send_message. invoke_subagent returns before the helper runs, and the main conversation's Stop can come before the helper's writes.

limits_and_timeouts.claim: A shell command that exits non-zero has an empty error and no output or exit code on PostToolUse, so it reads as a call that worked.

open_questions: Does the global ~/.gemini/config/hooks.json take the split entries (a group for tool events, a plain handler for the rest) as the workspace file does?
Does any event mark a new turn, so the prompt can be recorded once per turn?
Does a headless-denied call have any hook that fires after it?
Can any Antigravity hook block a step or rewrite its input? The recording sent no hook answers.
